content.text:
Your current source is the strongest final baseline: it exactly matches package `47e1f6ce6850`, which has two scored public runs at quality 100.

| 100-run family | Best cost×time | Key difference |
|---|---:|---|
| `8567…` | 270.7 | First valid 100 baseline |
| `385a…` | 545.1 | Courier loop/TAN protections |
| `146e…` | 322.4 | Candidate-fact and anti-loop improvements |
| `a956…` | 391.3 | Routing and recovery iteration |
| `b760…` | 187.3 | More aggressive stalled-action blocking |
| `b1a…` | 191.0 | Alternate aggressive wake/retry variant |
| `47e1…` (current) | **174.5** | Keeps routing + TAN protection, removes overly aggressive blocking |

Your linked [latest run](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/runs/run_6baaba90a873f7b1) is quality 100 with 184.0 cost×time. The earlier [run_44a626…](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/runs/run_44a626efbd537259) used the exact same code, also scored 100, and is your fastest result at 174.5.

The important finding: identical packages can still score low or fail when Qwen times out or the tender portal stops loading. So no code can honestly guarantee 100 “all the time” under an unavailable model/site. The current package is nonetheless the best evidence-backed choice: 2/2 scored runs at 100, while the other 100-point packages each also showed a low-score or no-answer run.

Recommendation: freeze the current [`starter-kit`](/D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit) as the final submission baseline. Do not merge the aggressive loop/stall controls from `b760`/`b1a`; they increased false stops. The next safe improvement is a separately tested, deadline-aware model retry policy for upstream outages—not any scenario-specific fallback.
